The **MKS Test** is used to identify the beginning of a trend in a time series:

- Null Hypothesis: There are no change points in the time series.
- Alternative Hypothesis: There are _one or more_ change points in the time series.

## Statistics

```{r, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE }

# Subset crossing_df on the statistically significant crossings
invisible(list2env(params, env = environment()))
crossing_df <- crossing_df[which(abs(crossing_df$statistic) > abs(bound)), ]

# Configure the message to inform the user of changepoints
if (nrow(crossing_df) == 0) {
	message1 <- " no"
	message2 <- "."
} else {
	message1 <- ""
	message2 <- glue(" at {toString(crossing_df$year)}.")
}

```

- P-value: `r round(params$p_value, 3)`
- Significance level: `r params$alpha`

Given the test statistic and p-value, we *`r params$outcome`* the null hypothesis.

There are`r message1` statistically significant change points`r message2`
